sentences.text:
Case :- Writ - C No. - 25528 of 2020
Petitioner :- Vidyanand Srivastava
Respondent :- State Of U.P.Thru Collector Raibareli And Anr.

Counsel for Petitioner :- Ram Nath Pandey,Pankaj Kumar Shukla Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.,Illegible Hon'ble Vivek Chaudhary,J.
Hon'ble Manish Kumar,J.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Petitioner has approached this Court for a Mandamus direction to Opposite Party No.2 to provide interest @ 18% per annum, upon the amount of compensation award from 2003 to 2019, in the interest of justice.
It has further been prayed to direct the Opposite Party No.2 to provide compensation according to circle rate for the land acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
Admittedly, the award with regard to the land of the petitioner was issued on 30.05.2009 and the petitioner had not filed any reference against the said order.

Therefore, at this stage, there cannot be Vidyanand Srivastava vs State Of U.P.Thru Collector Raibareli ... on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/135642795/

sentences.text: any modification / enhancement of the said award.
Next prayer of the petitioner is that he is entitled for the payment of interest @ 18 % per annum as after the award passed on 30.05.2009 the amount is paid to the petitioner in the year 2019.

Learned Standing Counsel by his counter affidavit placed on record the amount deposited through Challan No. D-10, dated 23.02.2012 could not be released in favour of the petitioner as the Union Bank of India, Branch- Raibareli by its letter dated 12.03.2010 had stopped payment of the amount of compensation as against the land of Khasra No.157 the tenure holder had taken a loan and thus the amount was to be paid directly to the Bank. Thus, the learned standing counsel states that due to the said reason the amount had not been paid to the petitioner earlier.
In the given circumstances, learned Standing Counsel states that the delay in payment has not occurred because of the state.

Looking into the disputed question of fact involved with regard to the liability of a person and the entitlement of the petitioner for interest, the writ petition is disposed of with liberty to the petitioner to file a civil suit with regard to the same.
[Manish Kumar,J.]
